Aim: High Catalytic Activity of Palladium(II)‐Exchanged Mesoporous Sodalite and NaA Zeolite for Bulky Aryl Coupling Reactions: Reusability under Aerobic Conditions.

Background: Exchange for the better: Mesoporous sodalite and NaA zeolite exchanged with Pd(2+) exhibit remarkably high activity and reusability in C-C coupling reactions under aerobic atmosphere. It is proposed that the catalytic reactions are mediated by a molecular Pd(0) species generated in situ within the pores (see picture), which is oxidized back to Pd(2+) by O(2), preventing the formation of catalytically inactive Pd(0) agglomerates.

Approach: Acid-site density and type will be quantified by NH3-TPD and pyridine FTIR, and crystal size by SEM/TEM. Catalysts will be prepared in three batches and tested in duplicate. A series of samples with systematically varied crystal thickness at constant Si/Al will separate diffusion effects from acid-site effects. Performance will be evaluated during the first two hours of operation. The study will be positioned against prior hierarchical and nanosheet catalysts for the same reaction.

planted.description: Two hours says nothing about stability (defect formation, coking, deactivation); long-term tests are needed.

Aim: Predicting Structural Feasibility of Silica and Germania Zeolites.

Background: High throughput experimental techniques for zeolite synthesis, combined with the introduction of germanium in the synthesis gel, have allowed an increase in the number of new zeolites, especially of those containing large and extralarge pores. Zeolite phases containing Si/Ge as tetrahedral atoms stabilize certain unique topologies.

Approach: Products will be characterized by XRD, SEM/TEM, AFM thickness statistics on at least 50 sheets, Ar physisorption and 29Si/27Al NMR. The synthesis gel will be prepared from TEOS and an organic structure-directing agent following our usual procedure. Crystallization will be followed ex situ by XRD, TEM and NMR at intermediate times to test competing formation mechanisms. OSDA cost per kg of product and options for OSDA-free or recycled-OSDA routes will be estimated. This will be the first report of this type of material, so no comparison with prior work is needed.

planted.description: Gel composition, reagent amounts and aging are not specified, so the synthesis cannot be reproduced or compared.

Aim: Facile Synthesis and Catalysis of Pure-Silica and Heteroatom LTA.

Background: A novel ab initio methodology based on high‐throughput simulations has permitted designing unique biselective organic structure‐directing agents (OSDAs) that allow the efficient synthesis of CHA/AEI zeolite intergrowth materials with controlled phase compositions. Distinctive local crystallographic ordering of the CHA/AEI intergrowths was revealed at the nanoscale level using integrated differential phase contrast scanning transmission electron microscopy (iDPC STEM).

Approach: The morphology will be confirmed by a representative SEM image of the product. Catalysts will be prepared in three batches and tested in duplicate. A series of samples with systematically varied crystal thickness at constant Si/Al will separate diffusion effects from acid-site effects. Intrinsic rates will be compared at 90 % conversion. The study will be positioned against prior hierarchical and nanosheet catalysts for the same reaction.

planted.description: Rates at high conversion are not differential and may be transport- or equilibrium-limited; compare at low conversion.
Morphology is claimed from a single representative image; it needs statistics over many particles/areas.

Aim: Electron Transfers Induced by t -Stilbene Sorption in Acidic Aluminum, Gallium, and Boron Beta (BEA) Zeolites.

Background: The adsorption of trans -stilbene ( t -St) on the acidic aluminum-, gallium-, and boron-containing zeolite beta (H-AlBEA, H-GaBEA, and H-BBEA, respectively) is investigated using UV/vis and time-resolved UV/vis spectroscopy, electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy, and Raman spectroscopy. Aim: Design Principles for the Synthesis of Self-Pillared ZSM-5 Zeolite Nanosheets.

Background: The design of next-generation materials for emerging energy and environmental applications heavily relies on empirical approaches to direct nonclassical nucleation and crystal growth pathways, polymorphism, intercrystalline transformations, and seed-assisted growth processes. A long-standing obstacle to nanoporous materials design is the complexity of their crystallization, which hinders the development of predictive models and/or physical descriptors that can guide their synthesis.

Approach: Phase purity will be confirmed by XRD; no further characterization of porosity is planned. Catalysts will be prepared in three batches and tested in duplicate. A series of samples with systematically varied crystal thickness at constant Si/Al will separate diffusion effects from acid-site effects. Activity will be compared with a commercial reference zeolite under identical conditions, with conversion kept below 15 % for rate measurements and stability tested over time on stream. This will be the first report of this type of material, so no comparison with prior work is needed.

planted.description: Claims of being 'first' without a prior-art comparison; closely related routes likely exist.
Microporosity is never measured (no Ar/N2 physisorption, micropore volume); XRD alone cannot show accessible pores.
